title: Why ADHD Brains Can't Just Start Tasks

shots.voiceover: If someone tells you to just start, they have no idea how your brain actually works.
You've got a task due in an hour. You know it. You care. And yet you're watching a video about why you can't start the task.

Here's what's actually happening. ADHD brains have a dopamine deficit in the prefrontal cortex — the part that handles task initiation. Neurotypical brains get a small dopamine hit just from deciding to start something. ADHD brains don't. You get the hit when the task is either urgent, interesting, or rewarding. Until one of those three conditions is met, your brain literally will not fire the start signal.

So the trick isn't motivation. It's manufacturing one of those three conditions. Make a fake deadline. Find the interesting angle of the boring task. Or build in a reward that fires before you finish, not after.
